findings.summary: The provenance acceptance still has no implementable attestation contract.
findings.rationale: The amendment requires every producer/invocation to resolve through a Host-issued or authenticated external attestation and validates issuer, expiry, replay protection, and role coverage, but defines no authorized issuer protocol, schema, key/discovery mechanism, or deterministic verification boundary. The Notes explicitly leave strong identity to the Host. Without a repository-owned contract, implementations can claim authentication while the verifier has no portable way to validate it.
findings.direction: Specify the attestation schema and trust boundary (issuer registry, signed claims/key resolution, expiry/replay checks, and authenticated-maintainer fallback) or explicitly narrow repository acceptance to validating host-provided evidence rather than asserting authentication.

findings.summary: Invocation uniqueness and retry semantics remain internally ambiguous.
findings.rationale: The packet says uniqueness is scoped to `(Work Item, Candidate, role)` while also requiring retries, branches, and replayed attestations to remain visible. It does not state whether multiple legitimate retries for the same role/Candidate are permitted, how they are ordered, or which one satisfies completion. A strict interpretation rejects valid retries; a permissive interpretation can admit repeated role execution or allow stale reports to be selected.
findings.direction: Define one role-attempt identity/index model: permit multiple attempts with unique attempt IDs, record supersession/failure explicitly, and define deterministic selection/completeness rules.

findings.summary: This Work Item is too broad and overlaps the dependent gauntlet/controller boundary.
findings.rationale: 05 owns role provenance, prompt registry, final-candidate transitions, canonical invalidation across verifier imports, QA sandbox materialization, hardener surface derivation, finding consolidation, unsupported-host recovery, orientation, and public workflow documentation. The next Work Item 08 separately owns the end-to-end stage controller and consolidated repair loop. That split leaves no tight independently deliverable slice and invites duplicated or conflicting transition logic.
findings.direction: Limit 05 to role contracts, manifests, attestation binding, and role-evidence verification; move controller transitions, repair-loop consolidation, invalidation orchestration, and workflow closeout to 08 with explicit interfaces.

residualRisks: The amended diff resolves the original small-change policy conflict by explicitly amending the exception.
The amended model-routing item resolves the prior classification gap with a fail-closed matrix and precedence requirement.
Host-dependent dogfood remains externally attestable rather than repository-proven.
